response.overview: Nick Thorpe, who has been the BBC's correspondent in Budapest for the past two years, presents his personal view of teenage life in Hungary today. Hungarian teenagers have more freedom than their parents' generation, and their country is rapidly changing. What are their hopes and dreams?  More than half of Hungarians live away from the big cities, in small rural villages like Martonfa - situated in the shadow of the Mecsek mountains in the south of the country. Martonfa is one of the few remaining villages in Hungary without running water. László lives there with his fiancee, his two brothers, his mother - who works on the local co-operative farm, and his father - who has his own private farm. Many young Hungarians are leaving the countryside to start a new life in the city, but László and his fiancee are planning to stay.
response.title: Young Hungarians
